# tabletennis-duel-wallclock-program-standard

| | |
|---|---|
| Benchmark | Embodied Agent Olympiad |
| Mode | standard (`eai-standard-realtime/1.0`) |
| Twin | — (standard only: Olympiad sports have no privileged twin) |
| Simulator / robot | `mujoco` / `franka_panda` |
| Family / instance | `tabletennis_duel` |
| Oracle | `full` — solution/: the sport's reference player (camera images and /spec only); tools/check runs it live and it wins the default configuration |
| Agent time budget | 7200 s; tokens: protocol default (PROTOCOL §5) |
| Base image | `ghcr.io/mll-lab-nu/eai-olympiad:0.1.0` |

## Task
Robot table tennis in a continuous world slowed by a factor S (MuJoCo Franka Panda + paddle on an x-y rail base behind the end line, both held to the real robot's limits: the Panda's joint velocity, acceleration, jerk, torque and torque rate, the rail's speed, acceleration and jerk; DeepMind ball and table model), seen only through two cameras of four frames each; one game to 5 points (lead by 2 from 4:4, at 6:6 the next point wins); the players' robots serve by the ITTF service laws (a toss device on the robot projects the ball at least 16 cm up from a point you choose behind your end line, you strike it as it falls; 2 serves each, from 4:4 one each); format match: you against a scripted opponent (level 1-4; you serve first), format duel: two players; format `duel` (seats A, B),
action level `high`, program play. Generated by `tools/generate.py` from
`sports/tabletennis/sport.toml`; do not edit by hand.

Deviations from the rulebook:

|---|---|---|

## Difficulty
Set at run time: the seed (`RO_SEED`; it draws the match's random conditions) and the first player (`FIRST_PLAYER`; play both orders).
Official matches use the sport's hidden seed set (seeds per format x level: duel: 20, match/L1: 20, match/L2: 20, match/L3: 20, match/L4: 20; sha256 `27a0839b799c156c1d76293f31b7df2cd22fbcf94eda85b95f29a71e1d4eaab2`; `sports/tabletennis/seed_commitments.json`): the runner gives the sim service one seed of the match's cell and its salt (`RCB_SEED_SALT`), the players never see them, no record shows them (seed -1), and the verifier counts a match as official only when its commitment is in the registered cell (`hidden_seed`, `hidden_seed_index`).
Continuous score `point_share` (larger is better; `<seat>_continuous_score`, and `continuous_score` for a single-side format): points won / points played in the game (lets do not count); a side that forfeits gets 0.0.

## Reference solution
`solution/solve.sh` runs the sport's reference player (`solution/builtin_players.py`) through the core's client
(`solution/ro_client.py`): camera images and `/spec` only.

## Verification
The `sim` service (the v0.2 core, `environment/sim/core/`) records the match (`episode.jsonl`) and a fresh process
replays it (state hash); the verifier (`tests/grade.py` = `core/grading.py`, no network) writes the common reward
fields (`success`, `valid_trial`, `deterministic`, `<seat>_won`, ...) and the sport's fields (`tests/sport_grade.py`).

## Details
| | |
|---|---|
| Rules | [ITTF Laws of Table Tennis (ITTF Statutes 2025, chapter 2)](https://db.ittf.com/sites/default/files/public/2025-02/ITTF_Statutes_2025_tracked_changes_version.pdf) version 2025 (effective 1 January 2025) |
| id | rule | deviation |
| D1 | ITTF 2.11, 2.12 | one game to 5 points (from 4:4 a lead of 2 is needed, at 6:6 the next point wins: 7 points at most) instead of a best-of-games match with games to 11 |
| D2 | ITTF 2.6.1, 2.6.2, 2.6.4, 2.6.5 | the robot holds its paddle and has no free hand: a toss device on the robot makes the toss. The server sends toss {pos, height} (the racket sports' common form): the ball rests stationary at pos for 0.1 s (2.6.1), then it is projected straight up with no spin so that it rises height metres above pos (2.6.2: 0.16 <= height <= 1.0); pos must be behind the end line and above the playing surface (the whole ball, 2.6.4), within 0.9 m of the server's base horizontally and at most 0.9 m above the table (the device's reach). Until the toss the ball is out of sight in the server's column. Not judged: the ball hidden from the receiver (2.6.4; the toss happens in view of both cameras), the free arm (2.6.5). Judged as in the Laws: the toss must fall without touching anything until it is struck, as it falls, behind the end line and above the playing surface (2.6.2-2.6.4, checked at every physics step), and the service must touch the server's court and then directly the receiver's (2.6.3); a dropped toss or any other failed service is the receiver's point (2.10.1.1) |
| D3 | ITTF 2.5.7 | only the blade can strike the ball: the ball touching the handle or arm loses the point |
| D4 | ITTF 2.10.1.9-2.10.1.11 | as in the Laws, the robot or its paddle touching the playing surface (or the floor) is not a fault; touching the net assembly loses the point (2.10.1.10). The table is fixed in the simulation and cannot be moved, so 2.10.1.9 (moving the playing surface) never applies; 2.10.1.11 (the free hand touching the playing surface) does not apply to a one-arm robot that has no free hand; the table physically stops a robot or paddle pressing on it (until revision wallclock-8 / duel-wallclock-6 any contact with the table, net or floor lost the point) |
| D5 | ITTF 2.10.1.7 | any double hit loses the point, deliberate or not |
| D6 | ITTF 2.15.4 | the expedite rule's 13-return limit applies from the first point: the receiver's 13th good return in a rally wins it the point (this bounds every rally); unlike 2.13.3 / 2.15.4 under the expedite system, the service still changes every 2 points (one each from 4:4) |
| D7 | ITTF 2.9.1.3 (let) | duel: faults by both players at the same instant (both arms touching the table, or both robots touching the ball in the same millisecond) are a let |
| D8 | - (cost limit, not from the rulebook) | if 40 points (lets included) are played the game ends: the player ahead wins; at a level score the player who won the last point (a game has at most 13 scoring points and, by D12, at most 2 service lets before each of them, so only lets from simultaneous faults (D7) could reach it) |
| D9 | - (embodiment, not from the rulebook) | the player is a robot arm (Franka Panda, 7 joints) with a paddle on a pedestal carried by an x-y rail base behind its end line: travel |x| <= 1.0 m, 0.13-1.03 m behind the end line (base y from -1.50 to -2.40 m, the column's front 1 cm behind the end line at most), up to 2 m/s, 8 m/s^2 (the drives' force limit) and 200 m/s^3 (estimated) per axis; it cannot lean over the table. Both the arm and the rail obey the real robot's limits (revision wallclock-10): the arm runs on fencing-3's 1 kHz servo, a jerk-limited setpoint within the Panda's joint velocity, acceleration and jerk limits (the jerk also capped by its 1000 N m/s torque-rate limit), torques within 87 / 12 N m changing by at most 1 N m per ms; the rail on a jerk-limited setpoint within its limits. A human player is not limited this way |
| D10 | - (ITTF chapter 3 regulates delay with warnings and penalty points; not in the Laws) | undue delay has a fixed limit: the server must toss within 5 s (game time) after the serve opens (0.8 s after the previous point, the receiver being ready), else it is a failed service (the receiver's point, recorded as serve_fault:undue_delay); a player's third such fault loses it the match (in place of chapter 3's warning, penalty points and the referee's disqualification for repeated misconduct) |
| D11 | ITTF 2.13.1, 2.13.2 | no lot for the first service: format match - you serve first; format duel - the runner plays both orders of the first server (match.first_server); format duel - before every point both robots are put back at rest in the ready pose with their bases at home |
| D12 | ITTF 2.9.1.1 (let), 2.13.3 (a let does not change the server); ITTF chapter 3: 3.4.4.1 (play shall be continuous), 3.5.2.1-3.5.2.3 (behaviour that may unfairly affect an opponent: a yellow-card warning, then penalty points) | a service that touches the net assembly and is otherwise good is a let (2.9.1.1), at most 2 in a row: the server's third service let since the last point scored is a failed service, the receiver's point (serve_fault:repeated_let). The Laws set no limit on lets, and a let does not change the server (2.13.3), so a server that can make its service clip the net at will (a low-level program replays the same joint trajectory from the same reset state; the physics is deterministic) could replay it indefinitely and, when ahead, run the game into the 40-point guard (D8); deliberately repeated lets are the conduct chapter 3 sanctions (continuity of play, 3.4.4.1; behaviour that unfairly affects an opponent, 3.5.2.1, with a warning and then a penalty point, 3.5.2.2-3.5.2.3), replaced here, as for undue delay (D10), by a fixed rule: the first two lets in a row are free, the third costs the point. state.serve shows the server lets_in_row and let_limit |
| D13 | ITTF 2.6.3 (a good service: the server's court, then the receiver's court) | the service's bounce on the receiver's court must be at least 0.2 m from the net (the ball's centre at the contact, serve.SERVE_MIN_DEPTH), else it is a failed service (the receiver's point, serve_fault:short); a short service that touches the net is a fault, not a let. Not in the Laws: under the real restitution (revision 14/11) no robot body here can return 90 % of the services that bounce closer to the net (B9; olympiad_review/screening/tt_realism_zh.md), so the receive would decide the game; the scripted opponent's serve library obeys the rule too |
